databases.name: DB_Prompt_Registry
databases.purpose: Stores, versions, and documents all system, user, and assistant prompts used in the Micro-SaaS.

databases.name: DB_AI_Models
databases.purpose: Maintains up-to-date pricing schemas (cost per 1M input/output tokens) for various LLM models.

databases.name: DB_Feature_Roadmap
databases.purpose: Tracks MVP features, execution status, and links them directly to the prompts and models they rely on.

databases.name: DB_Pricing_Tiers
databases.purpose: Models subscription tiers, calculating estimated margins based on projected API consumption per user.

databases.name: DB_Competitor_Intelligence
databases.purpose: Monitors competitor features, pricing structures, and positioning to find market gaps.

relations: DB_Prompt_Registry <-> DB_Feature_Roadmap (To link prompts to product features)
DB_Feature_Roadmap <-> DB_Pricing_Tiers (To track which features are in which tier)
DB_Pricing_Tiers <-> DB_AI_Models (To roll up model costs to subscription packages)
rollups: Rollup of Model Input Cost to Prompt Registry
Rollup of Model Output Cost to Prompt Registry
Rollup of Total Feature Cost to Pricing Tiers
views: SaaS Margin Analyzer (Table view with formula-based profitability indicators)

frequently_asked_questions.question: Do I need a paid Notion account to use this?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: No, this blueprint works perfectly on the free Notion plan.

frequently_asked_questions.question: Can it dynamically pull actual API costs from OpenAI or Anthropic?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: Notion doesn't support live API integrations natively, but we've built a pre-configured Models database with the latest pricing schemas that you can easily update in one click.

frequently_asked_questions.question: Is this suitable for non-technical founders?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: Absolutely. It bridges the gap between technical prompt engineering and business strategy, making it easy for both developers and no-code builders.
